title: Anthropic bans users from ‘needless abusive or cruel behavior’ towards Claude
key_facts: Anthropic has barred users from "sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior" toward its AI models, in an online usage policy.
The ban does not apply to common user frustrations, model testing or "dark creative themes".
The policy already restricted abusive conduct; Claude models can end a conversation if a user is persistently harmful, a feature launched last August as a model-welfare safeguard.
A spokesperson did not immediately say what counts as abusive or cruel.
Anthropic says it is "highly uncertain" about the moral status of Claude and other models.
Dario Amodei has said he cannot rule out machine consciousness; Sam Altman appears averse to the idea.
quote_evidence: Anthropic has barred users from exhibiting “sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior” toward its models, as the company’s leaders continue to ponder machine consciousness.
In an online user policy, the San Francisco-based company noted that its ban would not apply to common user frustrations, model testing or “dark creative themes”.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading AI lab treats mistreatment of its model as a policy matter while the question of AI moral status stays unresolved.
notes: Altman's X post quoted in the article was a response to a New York Times report on Anthropic leaders and religious scholars; it is background, not the subject of this story.
